title: Deciding MSO-definable choice on the infinite binary tree
formal: Given a monadic second-order formula phi(X,Y) over the full infinite binary tree, is it decidable whether there is an MSO formula theta(X,Y) defining a partial function with exactly the same domain as phi and with graph contained in phi?
definitions:
The tree domain is {0,1}*, including the empty word. Its signature contains the two labelled child relations child_0(u,u0) and child_1(u,u1), and equality. First-order variables range over nodes and monadic second-order variables over all subsets of nodes, finite or infinite. Formulas use Boolean connectives and quantification of either kind. The input has exactly the indicated two free set variables and no other free variables or external set parameters.

For each subset X, write R_X={Y:phi(X,Y) holds in this fixed tree}. A candidate theta must satisfy: for all X,Y, theta(X,Y) implies phi(X,Y); and for every X with R_X nonempty, there is exactly one subset Y satisfying theta(X,Y). When R_X is empty, theta has no witness. The same finite formula theta must work for all X. There is no causality, finite-state transducer, cardinality bound on R_X, or definability restriction on X. The decision algorithm is an ordinary Turing machine on formula syntax and must halt on every formula. It need only decide existence; producing theta is an optional stronger result.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked terminating decision algorithm and proof of equivalence to existence of the specified formula theta, or prove this existence problem undecidable. Showing that some relations lack uniformizers does not prove that recognizing the uniformizable relations is undecidable.
context: Rabinovich proves uniformization when every cross-section is finite and also exhibits strong obstructions for other relations. These structural results distinguish existence of uniformizers from the algorithmic recognition question.
why: Definable choice connects logical specification to the existence of uniform witnesses.

import_provenance.original_title: Deciding MSO-definable choice on the infinite binary tree
import_provenance.original_statement: Given a monadic second-order formula φ(X,Y) over the full infinite binary tree, is it decidable whether an MSO-definable function selects exactly one valid Y for each X for which any valid Y exists? Rabinovich proves positive uniformization results for finite cross-sections, but unrestricted relations remain the target.

context_blocks.text: Rabinovich proves uniformization when every cross-section is finite and also exhibits strong obstructions for other relations. These structural results distinguish existence of uniformizers from the algorithmic recognition question.

sentences: An MSO formula relates two arbitrary subsets of the infinite binary tree.
A uniformizer must select one valid output wherever any output exists.
The selection itself must be defined by a single MSO formula.
The task is to decide whether such a formula exists for a given relation.
Finite-cross-section results and examples without choice do not alone give that decision procedure.
